<description>
{
 "summary": "Updates CMake's `check_cxx_source_compiles_with_flags()` to treat compiler warnings as errors, cleans up compiler warning triggers across several feature detection snippets, and changes the x86 SHA-NI flag from `-msse4` to `-msse4.1`.",
 "problem": "When users or build environments pass warning flags such as `-Wall -Werror` via `APPEND_CXXFLAGS`, several CMake introspection snippets fail to compile due to unused variables, uninitialized reads, or implicit conversions, falsely disabling optimizations or failing configuration entirely. Additionally, `check_cxx_source_compiles_with_flags()` previously allowed warnings like `-Wunknown-argument` without failing, and the `clang-cl` compiler rejects `-msse4` even though x86 SHA-NI only requires SSE4.1.",
 "evidence": [
  "PR description demonstrates build configuration failure when passing `-DAPPEND_CXXFLAGS=\"-Wall -Werror\"`: 'CMake Error at cmake/module/TestAppendRequiredLibraries.cmake:91 (message): Cannot figure out how to use std::atomic.'",
  "PR description demonstrates ARMv8 SHA-NI detection failing under `-Werror=uninitialized` and SSE4.2 detection failing under `-Werror=conversion`",
  "Commit message for 5bb7c5646a: '-msse4 is merely a synonym for -msse4.2 in both GCC and Clang, but it is not accepted by the clang-cl frontend. Furthermore, the x86 SHA-NI code uses only SSE4.1 intrinsics and no SSE4.2 ones.'"
 ],

<category name="build" title="Build and CI">
## Covers

How the project is built, tested, and released: the CMake build system,
the depends system and its packages, Guix reproducible builds, CI
configuration and scripts, compiler and platform support, and the
tooling under contrib used for releases and development. Platform
labels (Windows, macOS) point here when the change is about building or
running on that platform rather than about a feature. The Build system
label is a strong prior.

Not build: source changes that happen to fix a compiler warning as a
side effect (they belong to their area).

## What matters here

Release integrity first: reproducibility of Guix builds, correctness of
dependency pinning and verification, and anything that could ship a
wrong binary. Then supported-platform breakage: a platform that fails
to build or run blocks users on it. Then CI reliability: flaky or
misleading jobs waste every contributor's time and hide real failures.
Then dependency transitions with deadlines (compiler or library minimum
versions, deprecations upstream). Then build time and contributor
friction.

Cosmetic CMake cleanups rank low unless they remove a recurring
breakage.
